previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic thrombotic disorder, COPD, and chronic pain presented with pleuritic chest pain and sudden right groin pain. He had not taken his home enoxaparin for two days prior to admission. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis. Imaging showed improvement in a prior aortic arch clot and no complications related to his IVC filter. The chest pain was determined to be atypical and non-cardiac, possibly related to a Spigelian hernia or musculoskeletal strain. Right leg pain improved spontaneously and was likely due to muscle spasm. His hypertension and COPD remained stable. Pain was managed with oxycodone as prescribed by his PCP. He was discharged home on his prior medications with follow-up arranged in hematology and with his primary care provider.
